134:     final int dimensionStart = resultRowHasTimestamp ? 1 : 0;
135:     final int aggregatorStart = dimensionStart + dimensions.size();
136:     final int postAggregatorStart = aggregatorStart + aggregators.size();

140:     }

143:     int dimPos = 0;
144:     while (dimsIter.hasNext() && results.hasNext()) {

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `ResultRow.populateFromCache` (processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/query/groupby/ResultRow.java:166): the post-aggregator restore loop never incremented `postPos`, so when restoring a groupBy result from the result-level cache each cached post-agg value overwrote the first post-agg slot — with multiple post-aggregators, later values clobbered earlier ones and remaining slots stayed null (exactly the reported `a2=31,548, a3=NULL` symptom).

The fix mirrors upstream PR #15402: iterate the post-agg specs with an incrementing index and throw a defensive `DruidException` if the cached object runs out of values.

Validation:
- `GroupByQueryQueryToolChestTest` (incl. the failing `testCacheStrategy` with two post-aggs): 20/20 pass
- `ResultRowTest`, `GroupByQueryConfigTest`: pass
- Server cache tests (`ResultLevelCachingQueryRunnerTest`, `CacheUtilTest`, `CachingQueryRunnerTest`, `CachingClusteredClientTest` 230/230): pass
- `GroupByQueryTest` errors were confirmed pre-existing on the unmodified tree (unrelated environment issue)
